model: Residential location: dwelling within the PUMA (two-level model, lower level)
purpose: Lower level of the two-level residential location model: which dwelling a moving household chooses within its destination PUMA.

data_sources.name: ACS PUMS 2014-2018 5-year, household and person files
data_sources.how: Download csv_h<st>.zip and csv_p<st>.zip for st = dc, de, md, pa, va, wv from the 2018 5-Year folder (CSV, not SAS). Variables used: SERIALNO, ST, PUMA, MIGPUMA, MIGSP, POWPUMA, POWSP, MIG, MV, RELP, AGEP, ESR, JWMNP, SCHG, NP, TYPE, BDSP, BLD, TEN, GRNTP, SMOCP, VALP, HINCP, VEH, YBL, WGTP; ADJINC (income adjustment) and ADJHSG (housing-cost adjustment) are columns of the same files.
notes: URL: the folder of the documented 2019 and 2024 5-Year files (2_silo/data_sources.md) with the year 2018: verify.
The package copy is 00_shared_data/acs_pums_2014_2018_5yr/ (project: ../inputs/pums_2018_5yr/). The package scripts read the package copy; replace its files by your download.

steps.what: input_check, part 1: keep a copy of the provided estimation and hold-out tables
steps.command: rm -rf provided_estimation provided_holdout && cp -R estimation provided_estimation && cp -R holdout provided_holdout

steps.what: Build the estimation and hold-out tables from the inputs (same random draws as the original run; asserts that the LL of the original run is reproduced on both halves)
input_check, part 2: compare the rebuilt tables with the provided ones (rows, column sums, largest difference); must print ALL TABLES MATCH
Log-likelihood at the reference coefficients (no estimation, nothing written); add --holdout for the hold-out sample
Biogeme estimation, start values = reference estimates
Compare the estimates with the reference (reference_estimates.csv)

notes: Sampled alternatives: the exact 30-dwelling sets of the original estimation (generator seed 20261117: first the estimation half, then the hold-out half), in the data; uniform sampling, no correction term.

Sample-size sensitivity (estimation half): with a second random draw of 30, and with 60 and 100 alternatives (each also redrawing the 200 dwellings of the PUMA inclusive value), no dwelling-level coefficient moves by more than 0.67 robust s.e. (0.57 with 60 and 100) and no PUMA-level coefficient by more than 0.34 s.e.; 30 alternatives are enough. Full table: output/sample_size_sensitivity_table.csv. In SILO the household sees 30 vacant dwellings drawn at random in the chosen PUMA (all if fewer).
Structure type SFD is the reference; ln income = ln(max(income, 5000) / 50000).
Bedroom need = min(household size, 5), chosen by fit among three standard rules and a rule-free form (see model/README.md).
The hold-out sample was also used in the specification search; its log-likelihood is not a fully independent test.
Steps with output_provided = true can be skipped: their results are in input/data or 00_shared_data. Upstream project stages were not re-run for this package; their runtimes are not measured.
Measured here: --evaluate 3 s, 1.1 GB; estimation 15 s, 3.3 GB (coefficients and robust s.e. equal to the reference to 4 decimals).
Environment: Biogeme scripts and the build script run with ~/.venvs/biogeme/bin/python (Biogeme 3.3.5); upstream project scripts with /opt/homebrew/anaconda3/bin/python3.
